![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/3439a263-75a3-4fcb-b202-79ed8d88187e-1.jpg?height=432&width=589&top_left_y=408&top_left_x=754)
Let \(R\) be the region in the first quadrant bounded by the graph of \(y=2 \sqrt{x}\), the horizontal line \(y=6\), and the \(y\)-axis, as shown in the figure above.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the area of \(R\).
\item[(b)] Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression that gives the volume of the solid generated when \(R\) is rotated about the horizontal line \(y=7\).
\item[(c)] Region \(R\) is the base of a solid. For each \(y\), where \(0 \leq y \leq 6\), the cross section of the solid taken perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis is a rectangle whose height is 3 times the length of its base in region \(R\). Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression that gives the volume of the solid.
\item[(a)] Area \(=\int_{0}^{9}(6-2 \sqrt{x}) d x=\left.\left(6 x-\frac{4}{3} x^{3 / 2}\right)\right|_{x=0} ^{x=9}=18\)
\item[(b)] Volume \(=\pi \int_{0}^{9}\left((7-2 \sqrt{x})^{2}-(7-6)^{2}\right) d x\)
\item[(c)] Solving \(y=2 \sqrt{x}\) for \(x\) yields \(x=\frac{y^{2}}{4}\).
Each rectangular cross section has area \(\left(3 \frac{y^{2}}{4}\right)\left(\frac{y^{2}}{4}\right)=\frac{3}{16} y^{4}\).
\[
\text { Volume }=\int_{0}^{6} \frac{3}{16} y^{4} d y
\]
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { antiderivative } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { limits and constant }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
